necessary_context.content: For each real x, H(y|x) is the distribution function of the scalar response Y(x); M(x)=integral y dH(y|x). Alpha is a given finite real target and theta a finite real root.
necessary_context.name: Response distribution and mean

necessary_context.content: There exists finite C>0 with Pr(|Y(x)|<=C)=1 for every real x. Starting from arbitrary constant x_1, the nonstationary Markov chain uses x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(alpha-y_n), with conditional distribution Pr(y_n<=y|x_n)=H(y|x_n).
necessary_context.name: Bounded observations and Markov recursion

necessary_context.content: The paper defines this as a fixed positive sequence satisfying 0<sum_{n>=1} a_n^2<infinity and sum_{n>=2} a_n/(a_1+...+a_{n-1})=infinity. It need not satisfy two-sided order 1/n bounds. The latter bounds, c'/n<=a_n<=c''/n for positive constants c',c'', are a sufficient subclass.
necessary_context.locator: printed pp.401,403–404, Eq.(6),(26),(30) and definition following Eq.(30)
necessary_context.name: Type 1/n

necessary_context.content: b_n=E[(x_n-theta)^2]; b=lim b_n. Theorem 2 assumes M is nondecreasing on R, M(theta)=alpha and an existing positive derivative M'(theta)>0.
necessary_context.name: Mean-square error and theorem conditions
